claims.claim: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek hand-powered orrery built in the 2nd century BC and discovered in 1901.
claims.excerpt: The Antikythera mechanism ( AN-tik-ih-THEER-ə, US also AN-ty-kih-) is an ancient Greek hand-powered orrery (model of the Solar System) built in the 2nd century BC and discovered in 1901.
claims.context: The device is identified as an ancient Greek orrery built in the second century BC and discovered in 1901.

claims.claim: It was among wreckage retrieved from a shipwreck off the coast of the Greek island Antikythera in 1901.
claims.excerpt: The artefact was among wreckage retrieved from a shipwreck off the coast of the Greek island Antikythera in 1901.
claims.context: The artefact was found in wreckage off the coast of Antikythera in 1901.

claims.claim: In 1902, the fragment was noticed by Greek politician Spyridon Stais as containing a gear.
claims.excerpt: In 1902, during a visit to the National Archaeological Museum in Athens, it was noticed by Greek politician Spyridon Stais as containing a gear, prompting the first study of the fragment by his cousin, Valerios Stais, the museum director.
claims.context: Spyridon Stais noticed a gear in the fragment in 1902, leading to a study by museum director Valerios Stais.

claims.claim: The device was found as one lump and later separated into three main fragments which are now divided into 82 separate fragments.
claims.excerpt: The device, housed in the remains of a wooden-framed case of (uncertain) overall size 34 cm × 18 cm × 9 cm (13.4 in × 7.1 in × 3.5 in), was found as one lump, later separated into three main fragments which are now divided into 82 separate fragments after conservation efforts.
claims.context: The mechanism was initially found as a single lump before conservation efforts divided it into 82 separate fragments.

claims.claim: Four of these fragments contain gears, while inscriptions are found on many others.
claims.excerpt: Four of these fragments contain gears, while inscriptions are found on many others.
claims.context: Physical examination shows that four fragments contain gears and many others contain inscriptions.

claims.claim: The largest gear is about 13 cm in diameter and originally had 223 teeth.
claims.excerpt: The largest gear is about 13 cm (5 in) in diameter and originally had 223 teeth.
claims.context: Measurements of the physical mechanism show the largest gear's diameter and original tooth count.

claims.claim: All these fragments of the mechanism are kept at the National Archaeological Museum.
claims.excerpt: All these fragments of the mechanism are kept at the National Archaeological Museum, along with reconstructions and replicas, to demonstrate how it may have looked and worked.
claims.context: The physical fragments are housed at the National Archaeological Museum alongside reconstructions and replicas.

claims.claim: Searches for items at the Antikythera wreck site in 2012 and 2015 yielded art objects and a second ship.
claims.excerpt: Two other searches for items at the Antikythera wreck site in 2012 and 2015 yielded art objects and a second ship which may be connected with the treasure ship on which the mechanism was found.
claims.context: Later archaeological searches at the wreck site in 2012 and 2015 recovered art objects and a second ship.
